correctness.rationale: The eight published characteristic-zero line equations exactly generate 28 seed intersections and 33 normalized integral lines. Exact enumeration produces 5,456 triple minors, of which 480 vanish, and the norm support of the other 4,976 is exactly {1,2,4,8,14,16,28,32,36,56,64,72}. This proves triple-matroid stability for every odd prime outside {3,7}. For the two remaining primes, a complete 528-pair projective-incidence grouping, computed over F9 and both F7 embeddings, proves the exact stated histograms and distinctness of 33 lines. Independent enumeration via the published 33-line table reproduces the results. The certificate is standard-library Python and relies on no samples for the universal assertion. Characteristic 2 and special-fiber freeness are expressly excluded.

evidence: General rank-three matroid specialization reduces to vanishing of 3-by-3 minors (cf. arXiv:2403.20024v1, Definition 2.3 and surrounding discussion of minors).
The published original supplies coefficient equations but no complete factor support of the 4,976 nonzero triple determinants.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General specialization theory implies only that the bad-prime set is finite. It does not determine the exact exceptional set {3,7}, prove absence of component collisions in those fibers, or give their point multiplicity profiles. No more comprehensive same-arrangement prime-by-prime classification was found.

The stronger general observation that triple determinants control matroid reduction does not imply the computed norm support or the exceptional tables. Closest known same-object published claim concerns geometric projective symmetry, not finite-characteristic matroid degeneration; possible unindexed computations remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: A complete good-reduction classification of the incidence lattice for a specific rigid 33-line free arrangement is a natural invariant, not an arbitrary finite-prime sample. The two special fibers exhibit distinct global incidence degenerations (169 generic points versus 89 or 57), while retaining all 33 components. This identifies the exact arithmetic boundary beyond which the complex intersection combinatorics transfers, relevant to positive-characteristic arrangement theory and matroid representability. No unsupported freeness statement is needed.
